note: A live end-to-end build: the requirements panel, then every build stage, on real models. All text was written by models.
brief: Work out when a distributor should reorder a product. The reorder point is the average daily sales times the supplier lead time in days, plus a safety stock of 20% of that lead-time demand. Recommend a reorder when stock on hand is at or below the reorder point.
facts: Made-up example: sells 50 a day, lead time 6 days: lead-time demand 300, safety stock 60, reorder point 360. Stock 360 recommends a reorder; stock 361 does not.

route.text:

Decision: the full panel. Two independent models check each other, and a person signs off at every gate.
A low-risk request, such as fixing a typo, would go to one model and a person, at a fraction of the cost.

panel.draftA:
REQ-1: The system calculates lead-time demand as average daily sales multiplied by supplier lead time in days.
REQ-2: The system calculates safety stock as 20% of lead-time demand.
REQ-3: The system calculates the reorder point as lead-time demand plus safety stock, which equals 1.2 times lead-time demand.
REQ-4: The system recommends a reorder when stock on hand is at or below the reorder point, and does not recommend one when stock is above it.
AC-1: Given average daily sales of 50 and a lead time of 6 days (a made-up example), lead-time demand is 300, safety stock is 60 and the reorder point is 360.
AC-2: Given a reorder point of 360 and stock on hand of 360, the system recommends a reorder, because stock is at the point.
AC-3: Given a reorder point of 360 and stock on hand of 361, the system does not recommend a reorder.
AC-4: Open question for the requester: the facts do not say how to round fractional safety stock or reorder points, or how to handle zero or missing sales and lead-time inputs. These must be confirmed before build.

reviewOfA.strengths: The draft matches the brief: lead-time demand is daily sales times lead time, safety stock is 20 percent, the example yields 300, 60 and 360, and reorder is recommended only at or below that point.

reviewOfB.strengths: The requirements faithfully restate the brief's formula and the at-or-below rule, and the acceptance criteria check both sides of the 360 threshold with correctly computed figures (50 x 6 = 300, 20 percent = 60, total 360).

build.contract: reorderCheck(input) where input = { averageDailySales, leadTimeDays, stockOnHand } (numbers; averageDailySales in units per day, leadTimeDays in days, stockOnHand in units). Returns { leadTimeDemand: number (units, averageDailySales times leadTimeDays), safetyStock: number (units, 0.2 times leadTimeDemand), reorderPoint: number (units, leadTimeDemand plus safetyStock), reorder: boolean (true when a reorder is recommended) }. Throws an Error whose message is "unknown field: <name>" if input has any other field. Numbers are returned unrounded; rounding and the handling of zero or missing inputs await OQ-1 and are not fixed by this contract. Example check: { averageDailySales: 50, leadTimeDays: 6, stockOnHand: 360 } returns { leadTimeDemand: 300, safetyStock: 60, reorderPoint: 360, reorder: true }, and the same input with stockOnHand: 361 returns reorder: false.

architecture.draft:
Component: one pure function reorderCheck(input) in a single module, with no I/O, no state and no dependencies.
Data in: { averageDailySales (units/day), leadTimeDays (days), stockOnHand (units) }. Any other key throws Error("unknown field: <name>"), checked before any calculation.
Steps: leadTimeDemand = averageDailySales * leadTimeDays (REQ-1); safetyStock = 0.2 * leadTimeDemand (REQ-2); reorderPoint = leadTimeDemand + safetyStock (REQ-3, equal to 1.2 x LTD); reorder = stockOnHand <= reorderPoint (REQ-4).
Data out: { leadTimeDemand, safetyStock, reorderPoint, reorder }, with numbers unrounded as the contract requires.
Number check: 50 x 6 = 300; 0.2 x 300 = 60; 300 + 60 = 360. Stock 360 <= 360 gives true; stock 361 gives false. This matches AC-1 to AC-3.
Risk: float error could flip the at-or-below boundary on non-integer inputs. The tests must assert exact 360 for the example. Any tolerance or rounding change waits on OQ-1.
Not built: rounding rules and the handling of zero or missing inputs (OQ-1). Do not add validation beyond the unknown-field check.
Tests: AC-1, AC-2 and AC-3, plus the unknown-field error case.
File fence (only these may change): src/reorderCheck.js (new) and test/reorderCheck.test.js (new). These paths are proposed, not given by the facts; confirm them against the repo layout.
No other files, configs or dependencies may change.
architecture.review:
No defects found.
Strengths: The pure function applies the PRD formula exactly: lead-time demand, 20 percent safety stock, reorder point as their sum, and reorder at or below that point, and the worked example matches AC-1 to AC-3.
architecture.final:
Architecture unchanged: the review raised no findings, so there is nothing to apply or decline.
Component: one pure function reorderCheck(input) in a single module, with no I/O, no state and no dependencies.
Data in: { averageDailySales (units/day), leadTimeDays (days), stockOnHand (units) }. Any other key throws Error("unknown field: <name>"), checked before any calculation.
Steps: leadTimeDemand = averageDailySales * leadTimeDays (REQ-1); safetyStock = 0.2 * leadTimeDemand (REQ-2); reorderPoint = leadTimeDemand + safetyStock (REQ-3, equal to 1.2 x LTD); reorder = stockOnHand <= reorderPoint (REQ-4).
Data out: { leadTimeDemand, safetyStock, reorderPoint, reorder }, with numbers unrounded as the contract requires.
Number check: 50 x 6 = 300; 0.2 x 300 = 60; 300 + 60 = 360. Stock 360 gives true and 361 gives false, matching AC-1 to AC-3. In double precision, 0.2 x 300 evaluates to exactly 60.
Risk: float error could flip the at-or-below boundary on non-integer inputs, so tests assert exactly 360 for the example. Any tolerance or rounding change waits on OQ-1.
Not built: rounding rules and the handling of zero or missing inputs (OQ-1). No validation is added beyond the unknown-field check.
Tests: AC-1, AC-2, AC-3 and the unknown-field error case.
File fence: only src/reorderCheck.js (new) and test/reorderCheck.test.js (new) may change. These paths are proposed, not given by the facts, so confirm them against the repo layout. No other files, configs or dependencies may change.

code.summary: The module is one pure function, reorderCheck(input), that follows the contract and architecture. It first rejects any field other than averageDailySales, leadTimeDays or stockOnHand by throwing Error("unknown field: <name>"), before any calculation runs. It then computes: lead-time demand = sales x lead time (REQ-1); safety stock = 0.2 x lead-time demand (REQ-2); reorder point = lead-time demand + safety stock (REQ-3). It sets reorder = stockOnHand <= reorderPoint (REQ-4). Numbers are returned unrounded. Checked against the made-up example: 50 x 6 = 300. 0.2 x 300 comes out as exactly 60 in double precision, because the representation error of about 3.3e-15 is below half the spacing between representable numbers near 60. 300 + 60 = 360, so stock 360 gives reorder true and 361 gives false, which meets AC-1 to AC-3. As the architecture specifies, there is no rounding, tolerance, or validation of zero or missing inputs; these wait on OQ-1. A null or non-object input is not guarded against.
code.review:
No defects found.
Strengths: Reorder math, the at-or-below stock test, unrounded results, and the exact unknown-field error all match the PRD and contract, including the 50-by-6 example.
